Below is a practical, evidence-based 12‑week strength + hypertrophy program tailored for a 26‑year‑old female recreational lifter on combined oral contraceptives (no cycle-based modifications needed). Start date: 2026‑06‑01. Program goals: increase maximal strength (primarily in squat, hinge, press, and press/row patterns) and improve body composition (increase lean mass, reduce fat). Assumptions: no injuries, cleared for full intensity, 3–5 training sessions/week available (I’ll provide 4 main weekly templates with two optional add-on sessions). If she can only train 3×/week, use the 3 most important sessions (Lower heavy, Upper heavy, Full/hybrid); if 5×/week, add the optional sessions as written.

Structure overview
- Duration: 12 weeks split into 3 phases (each 4 weeks): Foundation (weeks 1–4), Build (weeks 5–8), Peak/Intensity (weeks 9–12).
- Weekly frequency: 4 main sessions (Lower Strength, Upper Strength, Lower Hypertrophy, Upper Hypertrophy). Optional 1: Conditioning/Active Recovery; Optional 2: Mobility/core or weak-point work.
- Progression: Autoregulated weekly load increase based on RPE/Reps-in-Reserve (RIR). Deload in week 12 as a lower-volume week focused on consolidation and recovery (or if client prefers, move deload to week 8 and do an intensity block weeks 9–12; here we include a lighter week 12).
- Rep ranges: Strength sets use 3–6 reps (heavy), hypertrophy sets use 8–15 reps (moderate). Accessory/core 10–20 reps.
- Tempo: Mostly controlled 2‑0‑1 (eccentric 2s, pause 0s, concentric 1s) unless noted. Brisk concentric on power/contrast movements.
- Rest: Strength 2–4 min, Hypertrophy 60–90s, Accessories 30–60s.

Testing and baseline
- Before week 1 (ideally during week 0): establish 3–5 rep max (3RM or 5RM) for Back Squat, Deadlift (conventional or chosen variation), Bench Press and Barbell Row or Pull-Up progression. If unfamiliar, estimate 1RM via submax tests. Use these to set starting working weights (approx % ranges included below).
- Track bodyweight, tape measurements, and optionally progress photos every 4 weeks. Log all sessions.

Nutrition & recovery guidance (brief, practical)
- Calories: For body composition (lean mass gain while improving composition), aim for a slight calorie surplus of ~+150–250 kcal/day if primary goal is hypertrophy, or maintenance to slow recomposition if client prefers fat loss simultaneously. Because goals are strength + body composition, start at maintenance +100 kcal and adjust based on weight/composition change every 2 weeks.
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight/day. Prioritize ~25–40 g protein per meal across 3–4 meals.
- Carbs: Around training, ensure 1–2 g/kg in pre/post windows for performance; adjust fats to meet calorie targets (20–35% calories).
- Hydration: 2–3 L/day baseline, more on hot days / heavy sweat.
- Sleep: 7–9 hours/night. Prioritize consistent sleep hygiene for recovery and strength gains.
- Supplements (optional): Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day, daily multivitamin if needed, vitamin D if deficient, caffeine pre-training as tolerated (3–6 mg/kg if used).
- Recovery: Mobility 2–3×/week (10–15 min), active recovery days (walking, light cycling). Soft tissue work (foam rolling) as needed.
- Contraindications: none cycle-related; ensure safe warm-ups and progressive loading.

Progression rules (how to increase load)
- Strength lifts: add ~2.5–5 lb (1.25–2.5 kg) for upper-body lifts and 5–10 lb (2.5–5 kg) for lower-body lifts each successful week if target reps are met across all working sets with RPE ≤8. If a prescribed set misses reps, repeat same weight next session (or reduce 2.5–5%).
- Hypertrophy: increase load when upper rep target achieved across sets and RPE <8; otherwise add reps up to ceiling then increase load.
- Auto-regulate with RIR: keep 1–2 RIR for hypertrophy sets, 0–1 RIR for top strength sets.

Weekly layout (core 4 sessions)
- Day A — Lower Strength (heavy)
- Day B — Upper Strength (heavy)
- Day C — Lower Hypertrophy (volume)
- Day D — Upper Hypertrophy (volume)
- Optional Day E — Conditioning / Metabolic + Mobility (20–40 min)
- Optional Day F — Core / Prehab / Weak-point work (20–40 min)

Detailed 12-week plan
Phase 1 — Foundation (Weeks 1–4): Build movement quality, moderate volume, introduce progressive overload. Relative intensities start modestly to establish baseline.

Week 1 (start 2026‑06‑01)
Day A — Lower Strength
- Warm-up: 8–10 min total, dynamic hip/knee/ankle mobility, 2 light sets of squats
- Back Squat: 4 sets × 5 reps @ ~75% 1RM (2–3 RIR) Rest 2.5–3.5 min
- Romanian Deadlift: 3 × 6 @ moderate (focus hinge) Rest 2 min
- Bulgarian Split Squat (DB): 3 × 8 each leg Rest 90s
- Standing Calf Raise: 3 × 12–15 Rest 60s
- Core: Plank 3 × 30–45s

Day B — Upper Strength
- Warm-up: band pullaparts, scapular work, 2 light bench sets
- Bench Press: 4 × 5 @ ~75% 1RM Rest 2.5–3.5 min
- Barbell Row (or Chest-supported Row): 4 × 6 Rest 2 min
- Overhead Press (standing or seated): 3 × 6 Rest 2 min
- Face Pulls: 3 × 12–15 Rest 60s
- Farmer Carry: 2 × 40–60 m

Day C — Lower Hypertrophy
- Warm-up: mobility + 1 light set of each main movement
- Front Squat or Goblet Squat: 4 × 8–10 Rest 90–120s
- Deadlift (conventional or trap bar) light: 3 × 5 (technique, moderate) Rest 2–3 min
- Glute Bridge or Hip Thrust: 4 × 8–12 Rest 90s
- Walking Lunges (DB): 3 × 12 steps each leg Rest 60–90s
- Hamstring Curl (machine or Swiss ball): 3 × 12–15 Rest 60s

Day D — Upper Hypertrophy
- Warm-up: shoulder mobility, light rows
- Incline DB Press: 4 × 8–12 Rest 90s
- Lat Pulldown or Assisted Pull-up: 4 × 8–12 Rest 90s
- DB Lateral Raises superset with DB Curls: 3 × 12 / 3 × 10 Rest 60s
- Triceps Rope Pressdown: 3 × 12–15 Rest 60s
- Core: Hanging knee raises or lying leg raise 3 × 10–15

Optional Day E — Conditioning
- 20–30 min steady-state bike/rowing or 10 × 1 min hard / 1 min easy intervals. Finish with 10 min mobility.

Week 2
- Same template. Increase main strength loads by ~2.5–5% if Week 1 felt manageable. For accessory volume keep similar or add 1–2 reps per set if RPE <7.

Week 3
- Slightly bump intensity: Strength sets 4 × 4 @ ~77–80% 1RM. Hypertrophy maintain rep ranges and try to add 2.5–5% where appropriate.

Week 4
- Consolidation week — maintain loads but prioritize technique; keep total volume similar to week 1–3 but do not push to failure. This helps prepare for next phase.

Phase 2 — Build (Weeks 5–8): Increase intensity on strength lifts, raise volume on hypertrophy days. Focused overload.

Week 5
Day A — Lower Strength
- Back Squat: 5 × 5 @ ~78–82% 1RM (work towards top sets near 2 RIR)
- Deadlift (volume variant—conventional or trap): 3 × 5 @ 75–80% 1RM
- Bulgarian Split Squat: 3 × 8–10
- Calf raises 3 × 12–15
- Ab wheel or heavy plank 3 × 30s

Day B — Upper Strength
- Bench Press: 5 × 5 @ ~78–82% 1RM
- Barbell Row: 4 × 6 heavy
- Overhead Press: 4 × 5
- Pull-aparts / YTWLs: 3 × 10–12

Day C — Lower Hypertrophy
- Front Squat or Pause Back Squat: 4 × 6–8 (slightly heavier)
- Hip Thrust: 4 × 8–10
- Romanian Deadlift: 3 × 8
- Walking Lunges: 3 × 12
- Hamstring curl: 3 × 12–15

Day D — Upper Hypertrophy
- Incline Bench or DB Press: 4 × 8–10
- Weighted Pull-up / Assisted: 4 × 6–8 or Lat Pulldown 4 × 10
- Seated DB Press: 3 × 8–10
- Lateral Raises superset with Biceps: 3 × 12 / 3 × 10
- Triceps: 3 × 12–15

Weeks 6–7
- Progress by small weight increments each week on main lifts if target reps hit, or add one extra set on accessory work for added volume. Introduce one top set at lower reps (3–4) for squat/deadlift in week 7 to build maximal strength.

Week 8 — Recovery/Testing week
- Moderate volume, slightly reduced loads (85% of week 7 top sets) OR test a new 3–5RM on a chosen day if client feels recovered. If testing, ensure full warm-up and do only the lift being tested.

Phase 3 — Peak/Intensity (Weeks 9–12): Shift heavier and include heavier singles/doubles on strength days and higher intensity hypertrophy work. Week 12 is de-load/consolidation.

Week 9
Day A — Lower Strength (heavy)
- Back Squat: 5 × 3 @ ~85% 1RM (aim for 0–2 RIR)
- Deadlift: 4 × 3 @ 82–87% 1RM
- Bulgarian Split Squat or Step-ups: 3 × 8
- Glute Bridge or Hip Thrust: 3 × 8–10
- Core: heavy carries 2 × 40 m

Day B — Upper Strength
- Bench Press: 5 × 3 @ ~85% 1RM
- Barbell Row: 4 × 4 heavy
- Overhead Press: 4 × 4
- Accessory rotator cuff work: 3 × 12

Day C — Lower Hypertrophy (volume)
- Pause Front Squat or Goblet: 4 × 8
- Romanian Deadlift: 4 × 6–8
- Hip Thrust heavy: 4 × 6–8
- Reverse Lunges: 3 × 10 each leg
- Hamstring curl 3 × 12–15

Day D — Upper Hypertrophy (density)
- Incline DB Press or Close-grip bench: 4 × 6–8
- Pull-ups or Lat Pulldown: 4 × 6–8
- DB rows: 3 × 10
- Lateral raises superset with triceps: 3 × 12/12
- Core: Pallof press 3 × 12 each side

Week 10
- Add small increases on top sets (2.5–5% for upper, 5–7.5% for lower) if week 9 successful; include a heavy single for squat and bench at end of session (after warm-up) at ~90% for neuromuscular stimulus (no more than 1–2 singles).

Week 11
- Highest intensity week: squat/bench singles or heavy doubles (1–3 reps) at 90–95% 1RM depending on readiness. Reduce accessory volume slightly to prioritize recovery.

Week 12 — Deload / Consolidation (lighter week)
- Reduce total weekly volume by ~40–50% and intensities to 60–70% 1RM. Keep technique work and light strengthening. This week is to consolidate gains, recover, and prepare for retesting or next mesocycle.

Example session detail (sample progressive microcycle across 4 weeks)
- Back Squat progression example (if baseline 1RM = 100 kg):
  Week 1: 4 × 5 @ 75 kg
  Week 2: 4 × 5 @ 77.5 kg
  Week 3: 4 × 4 @ 80 kg (slightly heavier per plan)
  Week 4: 3 × 5 @ 75–77.5 kg (consolidate)
  Week 5: 5 × 5 @ 80 kg
  Week 6: 5 × 5 @ 82.5 kg
  Week 7: 5 × 3 @ 85 kg
  Week 8: Reduced or test
  Phase 3 weeks: peaking to singles at 90–95 kg then deload.

Conditioning and body composition notes
- Conditioning should be low interference with strength training. Prefer short interval sessions (HIIT) 1×/week or low-moderate steady-state 1–2×/week (20–30 min) depending on goals and recovery.
- If prioritizing fat loss: create a modest 250–350 kcal/day deficit while maintaining protein at 1.8–2.2 g/kg and not reducing load too much. If prioritizing strength/hypertrophy, keep slight surplus as noted earlier.
- Refeed / higher-carb days can be used on high-volume training days.

Sample weekly calendar (4 training day option)
- Monday: Day A — Lower Strength
- Tuesday: Mobility / light conditioning (optional)
- Wednesday: Day B — Upper Strength
- Thursday: Rest
- Friday: Day C — Lower Hypertrophy
- Saturday: Day D — Upper Hypertrophy
- Sunday: Rest or light conditioning

Coaching cues and injury-prevention
- Emphasize bracing during heavy sets (diaphragmatic breathing, tight core).
- Proper squat depth individualized to hip anatomy—aim for thighs parallel or slightly below if safe and pain-free.
- Pull hips back and maintain neutral spine during hinge/ deadlift.
- Monitor knee valgus on single‑leg work and reduce load/modify if present.
- Warm-up thoroughly before heavy days (general cardio 5–8 min + dynamic mobility + progressive ramp sets).

Testing and reassessment
- Re-test 3–5RM or estimated 1RM for the main lifts at the end of week 8 (optionally) or after week 12. Track body comp and adjust nutrition accordingly.
- Use session RPE and readiness questionnaires weekly to adjust load (if fatigue high, reduce volume by 10–20%).

If you want
- I can convert this into a printable week-by-week table, or
- Build a 3×/week or 5×/week specific schedule, or
- Tailor rep schemes more to specific lifts (e.g., Olympic lift variations, power work) or adjust nutrition targets to her bodyweight and activity level if you give me her current weight and goals (lose fat / gain muscle / both and preferred timeline).

Would you like a 12‑week PDF-style schedule laid out week-by-week with exact percentages based on estimated 1RM? If so, provide her current estimated 1RMs or submax lifts and approximate bodyweight.
